QuestionText: A device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy is a:
Explanation: An electric cell (or battery) contains chemicals that react to produce an electric current.

QuestionText: How many terminals does an electric cell have?
Explanation: An electric cell has two terminals: a positive terminal (usually a metal cap) and a negative terminal (usually a metal disc).

QuestionText: The thin wire inside an electric bulb that glows when current passes through it is called the:
Explanation: The filament gets very hot and emits light when an electric current passes through it.

QuestionText: An electric circuit is a continuous path through which:
Explanation: An electric circuit provides a complete, unbroken path for electricity to flow from one terminal of a power source to the other.

QuestionText: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them are called:
Explanation: Conductors, like copper and aluminum, allow electricity to flow easily through them.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an insulator?
Explanation: Rubber does not allow electric current to pass through it, making it an insulator.

QuestionText: What is the function of a switch in an electric circuit?
Options: To either break or complete the circuit
Explanation: A switch is a simple device that can either break the circuit (turning the device off) or complete it (turning it on).

QuestionText: If the filament of a bulb is broken, the bulb is said to be:
Explanation: A broken filament means the electrical path is broken. Such a bulb will not glow and is called a fused bulb.

QuestionText: Which direction is electric current conventionally assumed to flow in a circuit?
Options: From negative terminal to positive terminal
From positive terminal to negative terminal
From the bulb to the battery
Explanation: By convention, electric current is taken to flow from the positive terminal of the cell to the negative terminal.

QuestionText: Why are electrical wires usually covered with a layer of plastic or rubber?
Explanation: Plastic and rubber are insulators. They prevent current from leaking out and protect us from getting an electric shock.

QuestionText: You are testing materials in a circuit. You place a silver coin between the two free ends of the wire. What will happen to the bulb?
Options: It will not glow because silver is an insulator
It will glow because silver is a good conductor
Explanation: Silver is a metal and an excellent conductor of electricity, so it will complete the circuit and the bulb will glow.

QuestionText: A student connects two terminals of a cell directly with a single copper wire without any bulb or resistor in between. What is this condition called, and what will happen?
Options: Short circuit; the cell will get very hot and drain quickly
Series circuit; the wire will glow
Parallel circuit; the cell will charge
Explanation: Connecting the terminals directly creates a path of very low resistance (short circuit). A huge current flows, heating the wire and quickly draining the chemicals in the cell.

QuestionText: Air is generally a good:
Explanation: Air is an insulator. If air were a good conductor, electricity would flow directly through the air from plug sockets to us, causing constant shocks.

QuestionText: Why is distilled water considered an insulator, while tap water is a conductor?
Explanation: Pure (distilled) water has no free ions to carry charge. Tap water contains dissolved salts and minerals (ions), which conduct electricity.

QuestionText: Which part of a standard incandescent bulb acts as a support and connection for the filament inside the glass casing?
Options: The metal tip at the base
Explanation: The thin filament is supported by two thicker wires. One thick wire is connected to the metal casing, and the other to the metal tip at the base.

QuestionText: Electricians wear rubber gloves while working with electrical appliances because:
Options: Rubber gives a better grip on wires
Rubber is an insulator and protects them from shocks
Rubber is a conductor and grounds them
Explanation: Rubber is a strong insulator that prevents electrical current from passing into the electrician's body.

QuestionText: Which non-metal is an exceptionally good conductor of electricity?
Explanation: Graphite (the material used in pencil leads) is a form of carbon (a non-metal) but it has free electrons, making it a good conductor of electricity.

QuestionText: If a circuit has a battery, a bulb, and a switch in the 'OFF' position, the circuit is said to be:
Explanation: An 'OFF' switch breaks the continuity of the path. An incomplete path is called an open circuit.

QuestionText: A bulb has two terminals. Why are they structured such that they do not touch each other?
Options: To make the bulb look good
To prevent a short circuit inside the bulb base
To allow air to pass between them
Explanation: If the two terminals touched each other, the current would bypass the filament entirely, causing a short circuit.

QuestionText: Rohan makes a tester using a battery and an LED instead of a normal bulb. Why might an LED be better for testing some materials like lemon juice?
Options: LEDs require very little current to glow
LEDs only work with lemon juice
Explanation: Lemon juice is a weak conductor, so only a small current flows. A normal bulb might not get hot enough to glow, but an LED glows even with very weak currents.

QuestionText: Consider a circuit with a cell, a bulb, and a switch. A student replaces the connecting copper wire with a thick thread of cotton dipped in saltwater. What will happen when the switch is turned ON?
Options: The bulb will not glow at all
The bulb will glow dimly because saltwater is a weak conductor
The cotton thread will instantly catch fire
Explanation: Dry cotton is an insulator, but saltwater is an electrolyte (conductor). The saltwater-soaked thread will conduct electricity, but with higher resistance than a copper wire, leading to a dim glow.

QuestionText: In a torch, there are two cells placed one behind the other. How must they be aligned for the torch to work?
Options: Positive terminal of one touches positive of the other
Negative terminal of one touches negative of the other
Positive terminal of one touches negative of the other
They should be separated by a rubber disc
Explanation: To add up the voltage of the cells (series connection), they must be placed such that the positive terminal of one touches the negative terminal of the next.

QuestionText: A student builds a circuit with two identical bulbs connected end-to-end (in series) to a single battery. If one bulb fuses, what happens to the other bulb?
Options: It continues to glow with the same brightness
Explanation: In a series circuit, there is only one path for the current. If one bulb fuses, the path is broken (open circuit), and the current stops flowing everywhere. Thus, the other bulb goes out.

QuestionText: Which of the following would be the safest and most effective material to use to push away a person who is currently receiving a severe electric shock from a live wire?
Explanation: Dry wood is an insulator. Using bare hands, iron, or a wet towel (water conducts) would allow the current to pass into your body, shocking you as well.

QuestionText: Why is argon or nitrogen gas, rather than normal air (oxygen), filled inside the glass casing of an electric bulb?
Options: Oxygen would cause the hot filament to burn up (oxidize) instantly
Argon glows with a brighter color
Explanation: The filament gets extremely hot. If oxygen were present, the metal would immediately react with it (burn/oxidize) and break. Inert gases like argon prevent this.
